about.label: Core focus
about.text: Material selection, material characterisation, process–material relationships, mechanical properties, and failure analysis

blocks.text: A Materials Engineer studies, selects, develops, and tests materials to ensure they meet performance, safety, durability, and manufacturing requirements. In additive manufacturing, this includes understanding how material composition, powder or filament quality, printing parameters, and post-processing affect the properties of a printed component.

Depending on the employer, you might work with polymers, metals, ceramics, composites, or specialised materials. Typical responsibilities include analysing material defects, conducting mechanical tests, investigating failures, improving print quality, and qualifying materials for specific applications.
This role combines materials science, manufacturing processes, mechanical testing, microscopy, quality engineering, and data analysis.

blocks.label: Important distinction
blocks.text: Materials Engineer is a broad role. Some positions emphasise laboratory characterisation and research, while others focus on material qualification, supplier quality, manufacturing defects, or additive-manufacturing process development.

blocks.text: Year 1
Foundations
Build science and engineering fundamentals

items.text: Study engineering mathematics, physics, chemistry, and engineering mechanics.

blocks.text: metals, polymers, ceramics, and composites.

Learn CAD fundamentals and technical drawing.

blocks.text: Year 2
Materials science
Understand how materials behave

items.text: Study physical metallurgy, polymer science, phase diagrams, heat treatment, and material degradation.
Learn tensile, hardness, impact, and fatigue testing fundamentals.
Understand powder characteristics, filament properties, porosity, and material anisotropy.
Study additive-manufacturing methods such as material extrusion, vat photopolymerisation, powder bed fusion, and directed energy deposition.
Complete a mini-project comparing material properties or evaluating printed specimens.

blocks.text: Year 3
Characterisation
Connect printing parameters to material performance

items.text: Learn microstructure analysis, microscopy, material failure, and non-destructive testing fundamentals.
Understand how build orientation, layer thickness, porosity, scan strategy, and post-processing affect properties.
Explore thermal analysis, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and other characterisation methods where available.
Learn statistical analysis, design of experiments, and process–property correlation.
Seek an internship in materials testing, additive manufacturing, metallurgy, polymer processing, or quality engineering.

blocks.text: Year 4
Specialisation
Demonstrate material evaluation and problem-solving skills

items.text: Choose a specialisation such as metal additive manufacturing, polymer materials, composites, or material qualification.
Complete a project comparing material properties across print settings or post-processing conditions.
Learn how to document test methods, acceptance criteria, uncertainty, and results.
Build a portfolio containing experimental data, micrographs where available, plots, and engineering recommendations.
Apply for Materials Engineer, Materials Testing Engineer, Metallurgy Trainee, and Additive Manufacturing Materials Engineer roles.

blocks.label: Recommended final-year project
blocks.text: Effect of Additive Manufacturing Parameters on Material Properties.
Choose a suitable material and compare selected process conditions. Measure relevant properties, analyse the variation statistically, and explain the engineering implications.

Your final report should include the material specification, process parameters, test method, results, limitations, and recommendations. If you do not have access to laboratory equipment, use a documented public dataset and clearly identify it as secondary-data analysis.
Look for internships that expose you to materials testing, manufacturing processes, or material qualification.

blocks.text: During an internship, try to gain experience in at least one real test workflow—from preparing a sample and checking the method to interpreting results and documenting findings.

blocks.text: Useful standards to become familiar with include the ISO/ASTM 52900 terminology framework for additive manufacturing and the relevant material-specific test standards for tensile, hardness, fatigue, and other properties. The exact standard depends on the material, manufacturing method, and application.
A postgraduate degree may help for research-heavy materials roles, specialist characterisation work, and advanced materials development.

blocks.label: Recommended overall positioning
blocks.text: Present yourself as a materials-focused manufacturing engineer who understands how material composition, microstructure, and 3D-printing parameters influence component performance. The strongest starting combination is materials science, mechanical testing, additive-manufacturing fundamentals, and one well-documented project demonstrating how you evaluate and improve material properties.
